1) 从告警标签取 database_name 与 file_type，file: 1) Take database_name and file_type from the alert labels and handle file_type=LOG first, since slow log writes stall every commit; 2) On the host run iostat -x 1 and check that disk's await and %util to see whether it is saturated; 3) If the log file shares a disk with the data files, move the log to a dedicated low-latency disk; 4) Check whether backups, DBCC CHECKDB, or index rebuilds overlap the business peak and move them to off-peak hours.
1) 从告警标签取 database_name 与 logical_filena: 1) Take database_name and logical_filename from the alert labels to identify the slow file; 2) On the host run iostat -x 1 (Linux) or watch Avg. Disk sec/Read in Performance Monitor to tell slow storage from read amplification inside SQL Server; 3) If the storage is fine, optimise queries and add indexes as for page life expectancy to reduce physical reads; 4) If the storage really is slow, consider moving the file to SSD, splitting filegroups to spread IO, or checking whether backup jobs overlap the business peak.
1) 从告警标签取 instance（数据库名），执行 SELECT name,: 1) Take instance (the database name) from the alert labels and run SELECT name, log_reuse_wait_desc FROM sys.databases WHERE name = '<db>' to see why the log cannot be reused; 2) For LOG_BACKUP, run BACKUP LOG [db] TO DISK='...' immediately; this is by far the most common cause; 3) For ACTIVE_TRANSACTION, run DBCC OPENTRAN to find the long transaction and decide whether to KILL it; 4) For REPLICATION or AVAILABILITY_REPLICA, investigate whether replication/AlwaysOn synchronisation is stuck and repair the replication link first.
1) 从告警标签取 volume_mount_point，执行 SELECT D: 1) Take volume_mount_point from the alert labels and run SELECT DB_NAME(database_id), name, size*8/1024 AS size_mb FROM sys.master_files ORDER BY size DESC to find the largest files; 2) For an oversized log file, run BACKUP LOG to truncate it first and then DBCC SHRINKFILE; under the full recovery model it cannot shrink without a log backup; 3) If the data files genuinely need that space, clean up historical partitions or archive cold data; 4) As an emergency measure move tempdb or backup files to another volume, but plan a disk expansion.
1) 在数据库主机执行 systemctl status mssql-serve: 1) On the database host run systemctl status mssql-server (Linux) or Get-Service MSSQLSERVER (Windows) to check the service; 2) If the service is running, connect by hand with sqlcmd -S <host>,1433 -U <user> to separate a network problem, a port not listening, and a locked account; 3) If the service is down, check /var/opt/mssql/log/errorlog (Linux) or the SQL Server error log; a full disk, tempdb creation failure, or an expired certificate are common causes; 4) After recovery run SELECT name, state_desc FROM sys.databases to confirm every database is back ONLINE.
1) 执行 SELECT * FROM sys.dm_os_performanc: 1) Run SELECT * FROM sys.dm_os_performance_counters WHERE counter_name LIKE '%Page life%' to confirm the live value; 2) Run SELECT TOP 20 * FROM sys.dm_exec_query_stats ORDER BY total_logical_reads DESC to find the statements with the highest logical reads, usually full scans caused by missing indexes; 3) Take the suggestions from sys.dm_db_missing_index_details, review them, and create the indexes; this pays off faster than adding memory; 4) If queries are already optimised and it is still low, check whether max server memory is set too small or is being squeezed by other processes before adding RAM.
1) 执行 SELECT blocking_session_id, sessio: 1) Run SELECT blocking_session_id, session_id, wait_type, wait_time, wait_resource FROM sys.dm_exec_requests WHERE blocking_session_id <> 0 to find the head of the blocking chain; 2) For the head session use DBCC INPUTBUFFER(<spid>) or sys.dm_exec_sql_text to see what it is running; 3) Once confirmed as a runaway long transaction, run KILL <spid> to stop the bleeding; 4) Afterwards check whether that transaction lacks an index (widening the lock range) or the application forgot to commit, and consider enabling READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT to reduce reader/writer conflict.
1) 执行 SELECT name, state_desc FROM sys.d: 1) Run SELECT name, state_desc FROM sys.databases WHERE state_desc <> 'ONLINE' to identify the database; 2) Look for the most recent errors for that database in the SQL Server error log to tell an IO error from log corruption; 3) Restoring from the most recent good backup (RESTORE DATABASE) is the path with the least data loss and should be preferred; 4) Only if no backup exists should you use EMERGENCY mode plus DBCC CHECKDB(..., REPAIR_ALLOW_DATA_LOSS); that operation loses data, so take a file-level snapshot first.

1) Run SELECT name, state_desc FROM sys.databases WHERE state_desc = 'OFFLINE' to list the offline databases; 2) Confirm against the change record whether this is planned maintenance or a migration; 3) If unplanned, try ALTER DATABASE [db] SET ONLINE and read the error log for the exact reason if it fails; 4) Once online run DBCC CHECKDB([db]) WITH NO_INFOMSGS to confirm data consistency.
1) 执行 SELECT session_id, requested_memor: 1) Run SELECT session_id, requested_memory_kb, granted_memory_kb, wait_time_ms FROM sys.dm_exec_query_memory_grants to see who is waiting and who is holding; 2) For sessions with huge grants, pull the statement with sys.dm_exec_sql_text; it is usually a large sort or hash join, and a missing index amplifies the memory requirement significantly; 3) As an emergency measure KILL the largest consumer to release memory; 4) Longer term add the indexes suggested by dm_db_missing_index_details, split large queries, or raise max server memory.
1) 执行 system_health 扩展事件查询死锁图：SELECT XEv: 1) Query the system_health extended event session for the deadlock graph: SELECT XEvent.query('.') FROM (SELECT CAST(target_data AS XML) AS TargetData FROM sys.dm_xe_session_targets ...) and extract xml_deadlock_report; 2) Read the lock acquisition order and the indexes involved from the graph; 3) The usual fix is to make multi-table updates follow the same order everywhere in the application code, plus indexes on the participating queries to narrow the lock range; 4) In the short term the application can retry on error 1205, but that does not replace fixing the root cause.
Page Life Expectancy 低于 300 秒，说明数据页在缓冲池里: Page Life Expectancy has fallen below 300 seconds, meaning data pages are evicted from the buffer pool almost immediately. The instance is under clear memory pressure and physical reads will rise sharply.
SQL Server 事务日志使用率过高: SQL Server transaction log usage too high
SQL Server 存在 OFFLINE 状态的数据库: SQL Server has a database in OFFLINE state
SQL Server 存在 SUSPECT 状态的数据库: SQL Server has a database in SUSPECT state
SQL Server 存在等待内存授予的查询: SQL Server has queries waiting for memory grants
SQL Server 数据卷剩余空间不足: SQL Server data volume free space low
SQL Server 数据文件写延迟过高: SQL Server data file write latency too high
SQL Server 数据文件读延迟过高: SQL Server data file read latency too high
SQL Server 阻塞进程数过高: SQL Server blocked process count too high
SQL Server 页面生命周期过短: SQL Server page life expectancy too low
持续有超过 5 个进程处于阻塞状态，说明存在长事务持锁不放，被阻塞的业务请求会一: More than 5 processes have stayed blocked, which means a long transaction is holding locks. Blocked business requests wait until they time out.
数据文件平均单次写延迟超过 50 毫秒，事务提交会被拖慢，日志文件写慢时整个实例: Average per-write latency on data files exceeds 50 ms. Transaction commits are slowed, and when the log file is slow the whole instance's write throughput drops.
数据文件平均单次读延迟超过 50 毫秒（由 sys.dm_io_virtual_: Average per-read latency on data files exceeds 50 ms (derived from the cumulative io_stall_read_ms and num_of_reads in sys.dm_io_virtual_file_stats). Storage has become the bottleneck.
数据文件所在卷剩余空间已不足 10%，写满后数据库会停止写入，事务日志也无法增长: Free space on the volume holding the data files has fallen below 10%. Once it fills, the database stops accepting writes and the transaction log cannot grow either; this needs immediate action.
最近 10 分钟出现了死锁，SQL Server 会自动选一个事务作为牺牲品回滚: A deadlock occurred in the last 10 minutes. SQL Server automatically rolls back one transaction as the victim, so that business request has already failed.
有数据库处于 OFFLINE 状态，访问该库的应用会直接报错；若不是计划内维护，: A database is OFFLINE, so applications accessing it fail immediately. If this is not planned maintenance, someone took it offline by hand or a restore never completed.
有数据库处于 SUSPECT 状态，通常意味着数据文件或日志文件损坏、恢复失败，: A database is in SUSPECT state, which normally means the data or log files are corrupted or recovery failed. That database is completely inaccessible right now.
有查询在排队等待内存授予，说明查询工作区内存已耗尽，这些查询会一直挂起直到拿到内: Queries are queued waiting for a memory grant, which means the query workspace memory is exhausted. Those queries hang until they get memory, and users see requests stall.
该数据库的事务日志使用率已超过 85%，日志写满后所有写事务都会失败并报 900: This database's transaction log is more than 85% full. Once the log fills, every write transaction fails with error 9002.
采集端已连续 1 分钟无法在该实例上执行查询，实例可能已停止、监听端口不通或采集: The collector has been unable to run a query on this instance for 1 minute. The instance may be stopped, the listening port may be blocked, or the collection account may be disabled; applications will fail to connect.
